children: The South Korean won traded around 1,342 per dollar, reversing after touching its strongest level since October 2024, as a stronger US dollar and rising oil prices weighed on the currency.
The dollar index held near its highest level since April 2025, amid heightened geopolitical uncertainty and concerns over renewed inflationary pressures.
Oil prices extended their gains for a third session as fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia followed a deadly strike on Riyadh's airport.
Continued Russian strikes raised further questions over the energy truce with Ukraine.
Brent crude climbed above USD 106 per barrel, adding to concerns over South Korea's energy import bill.
Investors are also awaiting September US CPI data due this week for further clues on the Federal Reserve's policy outlook.
Meanwhile, continued dollar selling by local exporters, particularly semiconductor companies converting overseas earnings into won, helped limit the currency's retreat.

title: South Korean Won Retreats from 2-Year High
